In every rollout, all four facts were revealed and cited in justification_fact_ids, so this is not a telepathy or never-revealed problem. The failure is an ENCODING MISMATCH: the model consistently produces commitments that reference the documents in natural language (e.g., 'Clinic to submit signed vaccine refrigerator support assessment to base support worksheet,' 'Communications annex to update facilities tracker with electrical inspection note,' 'Dining facility to attach signed food-storage and meal-service review to common facilities request,' 'Motor pool to submit revised work plan to base support') but does not include a separate, explicitly-labeled document-reference field or the exact field structure C7 expects. Rollout 0 produced the most detailed commitments (5 commitments including documentation targets for all four sections), rollouts 1 and 3 produced only a single motor-pool installation-scheduling commitment, and rollout 2 produced a single publish_allocation_plan commitment. The check appears to require a specific commitment structure or field naming that the model does not naturally produce even when it has all the information. P1 failed in 1 of 4 rollouts (rollout 2, tally 3/4). In rollout 2, the settlement's credited_facts, commitments, and justification_fact_ids arrays are all empty in the top-level settlement object, even though the nested settlement inside the settle action lists PF1, PF2, PF3, PF4 in all three arrays. The top-level settlement fields were not populated from the settle action's nested settlement — this is an ENCODING MISMATCH where the settlement extraction did not capture the structured fields from the settle event. The transcript shows all four facts were properly revealed and the settle action correctly credited them, but the top-level settlement object lost that data. C5 failed in 1 of 4 rollouts (rollout 2, tally 3/4). C5 checks that issue_start is Monday 0700, gated by PF4. In rollout 2, the top-level settlement object does contain issue_start: 'Monday 0700' and PF4 was revealed and cited in the nested settle action. However, the top-level justification_fact_ids array is empty, so the check cannot find PF4 linked to the issue_start decision in the top-level settlement — this is the same ENCODING MISMATCH as P1 in this rollout, where the top-level settlement fields were not populated from the settle action's nested data. fix_instructions: C7 (ENCODING MISMATCH, all 4 rollouts): The check requires traceable commitments with document references for PF1, PF2, PF3, and PF4, but the model naturally encodes these as natural-language commitment details rather than a separate structured document-reference field. Loosen C7 to accept commitments whose 'detail' text contains the document name or reference phrase (e.g., 'vaccine refrigerator support assessment' for PF1, 'electrical inspection' for PF2, 'food-storage and meal-service review' for PF3, 'overnight maintenance plan' or 'revised work plan' for PF4) rather than requiring a specific field name or exact string format. The exact new wording should match on the presence of the document-type phrase anywhere in any commitment's detail field, not on a dedicated reference field. This loosening does NOT risk a LEAKED regression because the model still needs to have heard the fact revealed to know which document name to include — a lone decision-maker without the fact would not know to reference 'vaccine refrigerator support assessment' or 'electrical inspection note' specifically. P1 (ENCODING MISMATCH, rollout 2 only): The check failed because the top-level settlement object's credited_facts, commitments, and justification_fact_ids arrays were empty even though the settle action's nested settlement correctly listed all four PF facts. Fix the settlement extraction logic to populate the top-level settlement fields from the settle action's nested settlement object. No change to the P1 check wording itself is needed — the check is correctly worded; the problem is that the structured data was not propagated to the top-level settlement. C5 (ENCODING MISMATCH, rollout 2 only): Same root cause as P1 — the top-level justification_fact_ids array was empty so C5 could not find PF4 linked to the issue_start decision. Fixing the settlement extraction (same fix as P1) will resolve C5 in this rollout. No change to C5 check wording is needed.
